$comment: Vetted MCP servers this kit may configure. Only the ENTRY (what to run, when it applies) lives here; versions are resolved live from the npm registry at setup time and pinned in .ai/mcp.lock.json. Add your own in .ai/mcp-catalog.local.json (same shape; an entry with the same id overrides). Sources: npm | local-cli | command.

servers.label: Angular CLI
servers.why: Official Angular MCP server: best-practices guide, project listing, angular.dev docs search.
notes: Runs your project's own pinned @angular/cli (no extra package).
Started with --read-only; remove that flag only if you want code-modifying tools.

servers.label: Next.js DevTools
servers.why: Vercel's Next.js MCP: runtime errors, routes, and logs from the running dev server.
notes: Runtime tools need Next.js 16+ and a running dev server (npm run dev).
Sends anonymous telemetry by default; see the package README for the opt-out environment variable.

servers.label: Prisma CLI
servers.why: Prisma's local MCP server: migration status, migrate-dev, Prisma Studio.
notes: Opt-in only: exposes migrate-dev and migrate-reset (destructive). Use against a dev database.
Some Prisma 8 release candidates ship no `mcp` command (reported 2026-09-19); --verify catches that before anything is written.

servers.label: Context7 docs
servers.why: Current, version-specific library documentation, so agents stop relying on stale training data (AGENTS.md section 5).
notes: Third-party hosted service: library/topic queries leave your machine. Check your client's or employer's data policy.
Works without an API key; an optional key raises rate limits (pass it through an environment variable, never inline).

servers.label: Playwright browser + e2e
servers.why: Drive a real browser to exercise the UI, reproduce bugs, and write e2e tests.
notes: Not a security boundary: it controls a real browser. --isolated (set here) keeps each session's profile in memory.
Do not point it at browser sessions signed in to sensitive accounts.

servers.label: Chrome DevTools
servers.why: Performance traces, network and console inspection, Lighthouse audits in a live Chrome.
notes: Opt-in: exposes ~50 tools (context cost). Add --slim to runArgs for a 3-tool footprint.
Usage statistics and CrUX lookups are switched off by the flags set here.
Exposes browser content to the agent; officially supports Chrome / Chrome for Testing.
